sections.title: Posterior Capsule Rupture (PCR) Management
content: Signs: Sudden deepening/shallowing of AC, momentary pupillary dilation, nucleus falls away, marked slowing of phaco aspiration, visible torn capsule/vitreous gel.
Step 1: DON’T get out with phaco probe.
Step 2: Inject dispersive viscoelastic.
Step 3: If complete nucleus remains, convert to ECCE.
Step 4: If small residual fragments, phaco with low bottle height/low aspiration.
Step 5: If large fragments, visco-expression after extending main wound.
Step 6: Replug tear with dispersive OVD; fill AC with cohesive OVD; manual aspiration of residual cortex (irrigation off).
Step 7: Remove all vitreous from AC, wound, and tear using vitrector.
Step 8: Vitrector infusion high, cutter low.
Step 9: Visualize vitreous using 0.1ml of 40mg/ml Triamcinolone.
Step 10: PC IOL if small tear; 3-piece sulcus IOL if large (0.5D less if optic capture, 0.5-1D less if no optic capture).
Step 11: Pilocarpine to constrict pupil post-PC IOL or prior to AC IOL.
Step 12: AC IOL with iridectomy if insufficient capsular support.

sections.title: Management of Suprachoroidal Hemorrhage
content: 1. Immediate suture closure of incision.
2. Acetazolamide for pressure spike.
3. Topical/Systemic steroids.
4. Standard post-op antibiotics (Avoid NSAIDs/Antiplatelets).
5. Drainage of large unresolved hemorrhage after 7-14 days.
6. Completion of surgery after 1-2 weeks.

content: ANAPHYLAXIS: Secure airway, Adrenaline 0.5mg IM repeat q5m, Hydrocortisone 200mg IV.

DVT RISKS: Immobilization, Cancer, Estrogen, Obesity. Rx: LMWH + Warfarin (Target INR 2-3).
